Three API servers. One nightly Stripe reconciliation cron.

Two servers both thought they were leader. The batch ran twice. Rate limits hit. Duplicate customer emails.

Leader election and distributed locks — why "cron on every box" fails. 🧵

Some work parallelizes (stateless HTTP).

Some must run at most once cluster-wide:
• nightly billing
• schema migrations
• digest sends

Leader election = who coordinates?
Distributed lock = who enters this section now?

Split-brain = two nodes both think they're leader.

Classic cause: TTL lock + network partition + no quorum.

A still runs while B was elected. Duplicate cron, conflicting writes.

Mitigations: quorum (Raft), fencing tokens, stop work if lease renewal fails.

TTL locks fix crash safety — lock expires if holder dies.

New problem: holder pauses (GC) past TTL. B acquires. A wakes up still writing.

Fix: lease renewal tied to health + fencing tokens — storage rejects stale tokens.

Redis SET NX EX: fine for low-stakes, short, idempotent sweeps.

Sharp edges: no built-in fencing, clock skew, long sections, failover weirdness.

etcd/ZooKeeper/Consul when correctness earns dedicated infra.

Don't invent Raft.
